result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give similar fixes with concrete CSS. B is better because it opens by naming the core problem: group spacing doesn't show grouping, and borders add noise without fixing that. B also covers touch targets (44px rows) and has the container own the gaps, which avoids doubled spacing. A covers the same main fixes but treats the grouping problem as one bullet rather than the main point. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers handle all four rubric items well and give nearly the same values (24px between groups, 6–8px from title to items, 8/12px item padding, borders removed). A leads with the core problem, that the equal 4px spacing doesn't show grouping, and it adds a 44px touch-target option and container-owned gaps. B adds useful extras, such as a focus ring and the note that borders eat into padding, but it states the main diagnosis less prominently.
